<p style="text-align: center;"><strong><em>Updated August 2026</em></strong></p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center; line-height: 22px;">In 2015, Marriott International&rsquo;s Asia-Pacific revenue teams pulled numbers from <strong>five separate enterprise systems</strong> to answer daily pricing questions. Over <strong>five weeks</strong>, I consolidated <strong>73 data fields into four Tableau dashboards</strong> &mdash; one for each person with a decision to make. Here is how the project ran.</p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="30" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fa fa-solid fa-circle-arrow-down" show_icon="enable_icon" delim_line_color="#8224E31C" icon_color="#EEE6F6" icon_hover_color="#D4C9E0"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][vc_single_image image="53854" img_size="large" alignment="center" style="vc_box_rounded" onclick="link_image" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The project in one paragraph" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">What did the Datalabs Agency build for Marriott?</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">Between 2015 and 2016, the <strong>Datalabs Agency</strong> designed <strong>four production Tableau dashboards</strong> for Marriott International&rsquo;s Asia-Pacific operations, consolidating <strong>73 data fields from five enterprise systems</strong> into screens for General Managers, revenue managers, F&amp;B managers, and sales teams &mdash; alongside a dashboard design style guide and training materials.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The <strong>Datalabs Agency</strong> is a Melbourne-based data visualization consultancy founded in 2012 that delivers corporate training workshops (Power BI, Tableau, data storytelling), dashboard design, and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="1/4" offset="vc_col-lg-3 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Watch the data find its screen" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">From five systems to four screens</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Every metric a manager needs starts in one of <strong>five systems</strong> on the left and ends on one of <strong>four screens</strong> on the right.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The problem behind the brief" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">Why did Marriott need new dashboards?</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The animation above is the finished story. Before it, Marriott&rsquo;s APAC revenue managers were spending <strong>hours every week</strong> manually compiling reports from <strong>73 data fields</strong> spread across those five systems &mdash; MARSHA (reservations), Smith Travel Research (competitive intelligence), PeopleSOFT (financials), Sales Force One (corporate accounts), and GRMRS (revenue management). Basic questions took a compilation exercise to answer.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The questions themselves were simple ones: how is the property tracking against its competitive set this week, and should we discount rooms for the coming weekend? The data existed &mdash; the delay was in assembling it. APAC analytics leadership set a brief with a higher bar than reporting: they wanted dashboards that <strong>drove action</strong>, screens a manager would open on a Tuesday morning and price a room from. That brief shaped everything that follows on this page, from who was in the discovery workshops to why the final count was <strong>four dashboards</strong>, not one giant one.</p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][dfd_button button_text="Talk dashboards with us" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datalabsagency.com%2Fcontact-us%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-1"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Hong Kong, on site, with the users" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">How did the discovery workshops run?</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">I ran intensive discovery workshops on site in <strong>Hong Kong</strong> with the people who would actually use the system: revenue managers, General Managers, regional analytics teams, and executive leadership. From those sessions, <strong>four distinct decision-making contexts</strong> emerged &mdash; and each one became a dashboard.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The guiding principle: people are the ones who take action, so people come first in dashboard design. Insights come out of data, and they come out of the people working with it. It is the same co-design method I now teach in our <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/?page_id=661">team training workshops</a></strong> &mdash; the workshop is where you learn which numbers a decision actually turns on.</p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-table"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="One screen per decision-maker" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">The four Marriott dashboards</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Each dashboard was built around one user and the decisions that user makes.</strong></p>

<p style="text-align: left; font-size: 13px; font-style: italic; color: #8a8a95; margin-top: 10px;">All four shipped as production Tableau dashboards, integrating data from five enterprise systems.</p>

<p style="text-align: center;">Group &amp; Catering</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="10" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_single_image image="53866" img_size="large" alignment="center" style="vc_box_rounded" onclick="link_image"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Click the markers" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">Read the Hotel Dashboard like a GM</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Five markers explain what each region of the screen does for the <strong>person who opens it every morning</strong>.</p>

subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">One dashboard system, six tiers deep</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The four screens are not four separate projects &mdash; they are one system. This relational map from the project&rsquo;s dashboard design style guide from the project&rsquo;s dashboard design style guide shows how the executive summary rolls down through <strong>continent, area, market, and hotel</strong> to the four operational dashboards, supporting a <strong>six-tier organisational hierarchy</strong> with drill-down and filtering at every level.</p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_single_image image="53857" img_size="full" alignment="center" style="vc_box_rounded" onclick="link_image"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/6"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The rules under every screen" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">The design concepts behind the screens</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Six principles from the project&rsquo;s <strong>dashboard design style guide</strong> shaped every screen &mdash; and the guide itself became a deliverable.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-2"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Delivered, documented, taught" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">What did Marriott receive at the end?</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">Marriott received <strong>four production Tableau dashboards</strong>, a <strong>dashboard design style guide</strong>, and <strong>training materials</strong> for the teams who would live in the screens. The work was presented to Marriott&rsquo;s Chief Marketing &amp; Sales Officer and leadership team.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The style guide and training are the part that keeps paying after the consultant leaves. A dashboard is one artefact; a documented design language plus a trained team is the ability to make the next twenty artefacts in-house. That capability-building layer has been part of every <strong>Datalabs Agency</strong> dashboard project since.</p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][new_testimonials main_style="style-1" main_layout="layout-1" image="24350" author="Otto Ottinger" subtitle="The design principle behind the Marriott project" title_font_options="tag:h4" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|color:%23ffffff" description="People are the only ones who take action &mdash; so people, not data, have to be the priority in dashboard design." content_font_options="line_height:22" thumb_radius="20" thumb_color="rgba(81,86,52,0.46)"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" el_id="pat-faq"][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text css="" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]
<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Qwigley; font-size: 36pt;">Questions &amp; Answers</span></p>

<h2 style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: 'Bebas Neue'; font-size: 36pt;">The Marriott project</span></h2>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="How long did the Marriott dashboard project take?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Five weeks, delivered across Hong Kong and Melbourne in 2015&ndash;2016. Discovery workshops ran on site in Hong Kong; design and build ran from Melbourne, with the final work presented to Marriott&rsquo;s Chief Marketing &amp; Sales Officer and leadership team.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What tools were used to build the Marriott dashboards?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Tableau. The four dashboards consolidated 73 data fields from five enterprise systems &mdash; reservations, competitive intelligence, financials, corporate accounts, and revenue management &mdash; into production Tableau screens.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What was the hardest part of the design?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Deciding what not to show. With 73 available fields, the temptation is one enormous dashboard for everyone. The discovery workshops surfaced four distinct decision-making contexts, and each got its own focused screen instead &mdash; General Managers, revenue managers, F&amp;B managers, and sales teams each see what their decisions turn on.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Did Marriott&rsquo;s teams get training as part of the project?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Yes. The engagement included a dashboard design style guide and training materials, so Marriott&rsquo;s own teams could extend the system without depending on a consultant. Capability building is part of every Datalabs Agency dashboard project.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can the Datalabs Agency do the same for my company?" tab_id="1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Yes. The same engagement shape &mdash; discovery workshops with your real users, focused dashboard design, then a style guide and training &mdash; is how our dashboard design service runs today, for Power BI as well as Tableau. Start with the enquiry form on this page.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Ask about your project" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datalabsagency.com%2Fcontact-us%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1691550358421{background-color: #2f2e3a !important;}" el_id="pat-article-1"][vc_column width="1/6"][/vc_column][vc_column width="4/6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="People first, pixels second" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]
<p style="text-align: center;">Why the workshops came before the wireframes</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">I did not open Tableau in week one. I got on a plane to <strong>Hong Kong</strong> and sat in rooms with the people the dashboards were for &mdash; <strong>revenue managers, General Managers, regional analytics teams</strong>, and the executives they report to. Every hour of those workshops saved days of redesign later.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The workshops did one job: they surfaced how decisions actually get made. A General Manager checks the property&rsquo;s position in its competitive set before the morning stand-up. A revenue manager decides whether to discount a weekend based on pace against projection. Those are <strong>different decisions on different rhythms</strong>, and no single screen serves both well.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">That is why the number four matters. Four dashboards was not a design flourish &mdash; it was the number of <strong>distinct decision-making contexts</strong> the workshops uncovered. Each screen answers one person&rsquo;s questions completely, and nobody scrolls past someone else&rsquo;s numbers to find their own.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">I run the same discovery method today, in client projects and in our <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/?page_id=661">data visualisation training workshops</a></strong>. If you take one thing from this case study, take the sequence: <strong>workshops, then wireframes</strong>. The data model can wait a fortnight; the people cannot be skipped.</p>

<p style="text-align: center;">What Marriott taught me about design systems</p>
[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">Consulting with <strong>Marriott Hotels</strong> in Hong Kong in the early days of the BI revolution, I saw the problem that would shape the next decade of my work: dashboards were being created without a design philosophy, without a common design language, and without proper attention to <strong>colour theory, typography, grid systems</strong>, and <strong>user experience design</strong>.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">Four dashboards for one region of one hotel group already needed consistency &mdash; shared colour logic, shared chart conventions, shared naming. Scale that to a global company and the need becomes a document. That is why the Marriott engagement shipped with a <strong>dashboard design style guide</strong>, and why the deliverable list included training materials for the teams who would inherit the system.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">That insight became a core <strong>Datalabs Agency</strong> service. My <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/?page_id=394">data visualization style guides</a></strong> now operate inside companies such as <strong>Mercedes-Benz</strong> in Germany, <strong>Intel</strong> in San Francisco, and <strong>BlackRock</strong> in New York &mdash; each one doing for a whole organisation what the Marriott guide did for one region.</p>
<p style="line-height: 22px; text-align: left;">The through-line from 2015 to now is the same: a dashboard is a product, and products need design systems. If your organisation is accumulating dashboards faster than it is accumulating design decisions, our <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/?page_id=53840">dashboard design services</a></strong> page shows how we run that engagement today.</p>
